clue.text: Entrance part of party crowd in gilded ball

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: the crowd sits inside the gilded ball, cutting it open

parts.note: an orb is the golden ball carried as part of royal regalia
a jam is a crush or crowd of people

explanation.surface: A rowdy throng packed into a glittering ballroom party.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical post at the side of a doorway is a structural component of an entrance.

clue.text: Lover's part in Swedish erotica

indicators.note: only a portion of the words Swedish erotica is taken, the letters sitting within them

explanation.surface: A role in a piece of Scandinavian smut.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero, priestess of Aphrodite, was the lover of Leander, who swam the Hellespont nightly to reach her; she is the first of many classical and literary lovers in this themed puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Hero is the beloved of Leander, a famous mythical lover.

clue.text: Follow around flipping idiot in love

indicators.note: the word for follow goes round the other piece

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for idiot over so it reads backwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Someone trailing after a besotted fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads like a mild British oath aimed at 'idiot', but here it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being infatuated, showing excessive fondness, is the state of being smitten.

clue.text: Suitor admitting, say, what he wants?

indicators.note: the suitor lets the abbreviation in, holding it inside

parts.note: a lover is a suitor or wooer
eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A suitor letting slip, for instance, what he is really after.
explanation.walkthrough: LEG-OVER is British slang for sex; the definition works with the surface, as the thing the suitor is after.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude British slang for an act of sexual intercourse, which the suitor in the surface is presumed to desire.

clue.text: Lover with nothing on makes a bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece on another sits above it, so the zero comes first

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
Leander was the legendary lover of Hero, swimming the Hellespont to see her

explanation.surface: A naked lover commits a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder (British for a silly mistake), but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a flowering shrub, so it is a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Supports two boys one dates half-heartedly

parts.note: Pat is a boy's name, the first of the two
Ron is a boy's name, the second of the two
I, the Roman numeral, means one

indicators.note: half of the heart of the word for dates, one of its middle pair of letters, is removed

parts.note: someone who sees another person is dating them

explanation.surface: Someone backing two lads, one of whom goes out with people unenthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: SEES has two middle letters, EE; losing one of them is half its heart, leaving SES.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise a shop or artist is to support them as a customer or sponsor.

clue.text: Lover introducing the verse from Larkin?

parts.note: Philip Larkin's poem is titled ... The Verse, so the answer is the words that come before the verse in that title

explanation.surface: A lover reciting a stanza from the poet Philip Larkin.
explanation.walkthrough: Larkin's poem 'This Be The Verse' begins its title with the two words that run together to make the answer; 'introducing' says those words precede 'the verse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thisbe is the lover of Pyramus in Ovid, the pair whose story Shakespeare's mechanicals stage.

clue.text: See setter embracing individuals lacking love

indicators.note: the first two pieces hold the individuals inside them

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ones are single individuals
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch the setter hugging people who have no partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts the individuals between the first two letters of the word for see, not around the setter alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a sweetheart is lonely and solitary, feeling isolated for want of affection.

clue.text: Reluctant lover's initial vow

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word lover is taken

parts.note: an oath is a solemn vow

explanation.surface: A hesitant suitor's first pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unwilling to do something is a direct synonym for being disinclined.

clue.text: Funny person brings forward time for threesome

indicators.note: the letter for time is moved to the front of the word

parts.note: a riot is a hilarious person, as in 'she's a riot'

explanation.surface: A comedian schedules a three-way encounter earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three people, musicians or things is a trio; threesome is a synonym.

clue.text: Lover's vow shocked artless female lover

parts.note: I do is the vow said by a person marrying at the altar

indicators.note: the letters of artless are thrown into disorder, as if jolted

explanation.surface: A naive woman is jolted by a suitor's marriage promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who worships idols, or adores someone excessively, is a female devotee or lover.

clue.text: Playboy or Spooner's certifiable criminal?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: someone certifiable is mad
a lag is a convict or habitual criminal

explanation.surface: A men's magazine likened to an insane offender.
explanation.walkthrough: Playboy is the name of a men's magazine, an example of a lads' mag (British slang for such a magazine).
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy is a well-known men's magazine, an example of the genre called lads' mags.

clue.text: Married slim girl with a fluctuating weight

indicators.note: the letters vary and shift around, making a new order

explanation.surface: A wife who is slender sees her weight going up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluctuating' looks attached to 'weight' but it shuffles SLIMGIRLA into ILLIGRAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousandths of a gram are a measure of mass, so a quantity in these units is a weight.

clue.text: Risk passion, following break-up

indicators.note: the word for passion comes after the other piece

parts.note: an end is the break-up of a relationship
anger is a strong passion

explanation.surface: Rage after a split puts someone in jeopardy.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something in danger is to risk or imperil it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Japanese leader with fat lover

parts.note: Shinzo Abe was the Japanese prime minister when the puzzle appeared
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Japan's premier with a plump sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese leader' tempts one to take the first letter, J, but it is Shinzo Abe, then prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard, the medieval philosopher, was the famous paramour of Heloise.

clue.text: Again, do up rogue's clothing, about to pinch bum

indicators.note: the letters gathered so far grip the bum between them
the clothing of a word is its outer layer, the first and last letters

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a topic
butt is slang for bottom or bum

explanation.surface: Refastening a scoundrel's garments while about to grope his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' takes the outside letters of 'rogue's'; 'to pinch' has those letters plus the word for about grip the bum from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten a garment's buttons once more is to do it up a second time.

clue.text: Lover in transit, on the move

indicators.note: the letters of transit are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A sweetheart travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan is the knight of Arthurian romance who loved Isolde, a famous legendary lover.

clue.text: A warning about lubricant: it gives you a lift

indicators.note: about turns the warning round so it reads backwards

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: A caution regarding grease, which apparently cheers you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives you a lift' sounds like cheering up, but it is aerodynamic lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing-shaped surface produces upward force as air flows over it, keeping aircraft aloft.

clue.text: Shortly accepting ordinary kind of love

indicators.note: the word for shortly takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: speaking curtly is speaking shortly or brusquely

explanation.surface: A brief welcome given to an everyday sort of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective that completes a phrase: courtly love is the medieval tradition of chivalrous devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval ideal of chivalric, idealised devotion to a lady is known by this adjective.

clue.text: Italian lover: see one repeatedly be so frisky

indicators.note: the pair of letters is given twice over

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced like the word see
I, the Roman numeral, is one

indicators.note: the letters of be so are lively and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch an Italian lover being playful.
explanation.definitionFit: In 18th-century Italy this was the recognised escort and gallant of a married woman.

clue.text: One playing lute's a lover

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, is one

indicators.note: the letters of lute's are played around with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A lute player is someone's sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Iseult, or Isolde, is the Irish princess beloved of Tristan in the medieval romance.

clue.text: Drugs blocking awful feeling of lover

indicators.note: the drugs sit in the middle of the other word, blocking it

parts.note: dire means awful
Es are ecstasy tablets, so drugs

explanation.surface: Narcotics obstruct a lover's terrible emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Longing or passionate craving is the emotion felt by someone in love.

clue.text: Maybe sleeping around leads to tense, edgy argument

indicators.note: the word for in bed is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: abed means in bed, maybe sleeping

indicators.note: the leading letters of tense and edgy are taken

explanation.surface: Bed-hopping causes strained, nervous quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the word for in bed backwards; 'Maybe' admits that being in bed is only possibly sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal discussion of opposing views is an argument or dispute.

clue.text: Try dry fleece worn by hot, dishy type

indicators.note: the hot letter wears the fleece next to it, in a charade

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
TT means teetotal, so dry
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
to fleece someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: Someone tries drying a fleece worn by an attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a garment, but it means swindle, ROB.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishy person is good-looking, and a heart-throb is someone others find very attractive.

clue.text: Attractive Polish lover

definitions.meaning: a ... is an enthusiast or lover of something, as in film ...

explanation.surface: A good-looking lover from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to suggest Poland, but it is the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: well-muscled and fit, to shine by rubbing, and an aficionado of a hobby.

clue.text: Lover picked up ribbon

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a bow is a ribbon tied in loops

explanation.surface: A sweetheart retrieved a ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer, so a lover.

clue.text: Endless waiting to get 4?

parts.note: the answer to 4 down is leg-over; split as wordplay, leg is a limb and over is O, the cricket abbreviation

explanation.surface: Interminable waiting for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as LIMB + O: LIMB is a leg, O is cricket shorthand for an over, so it spells the 4-down entry. An over in cricket is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is an uncertain state of indefinite delay, neglected or waiting for a decision.

clue.text: Lover in group styled hair before ball

indicators.note: the rearranged hair comes before the ball

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

indicators.note: the hair is styled, arranged into a new order

parts.note: O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A seducer among a crowd, hair coiffed before going to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but it is just the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario is the seducer in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent, so a womaniser or lover.
